caps: When Hurricane Helene hit North Carolina, the water came fast.
The appeals came faster.
Hundreds of people asked for help.
Most were genuine.
But some were scams, chasing the same kindness.
Officials warned donors to be careful, but donors had no way to tell who was real.
So how do you give safely?
Now, with PayPal, it's possible.
This is Lifeline.
Every dollar finds the flood.
Paste any appeal.
Six agents check it.
The AI only reads.
Code decides.
Jess posted from Marshall two days after the French Broad came through town.
Marshall, North Carolina.
The Census finds the town, FEMA confirms the disaster, and satellite radar shows flood water a quarter of a kilometre away.
Verified: the disaster, the place and the local charities check out.
We never verify the stranger who posted it, and that's exactly why they're never paid.
Now the donor gives.
PayPal authorizes the gift, but doesn't charge it yet.
Only when every check passes is it captured, then split with PayPal Payouts across three registered local charities.
And if you want to help one specific family, add an optional follow-up request with a link to their post.
It's a request to the charity, not a directed gift.
They check on the family first and decide how to help.
The money is split, every receipt is hashed, and the person who posted gets nothing.
This is only possible with PayPal: authorize without charging, capture only when the evidence passes, split to local charities, or void, and the donor is never charged.
Now an appeal from Raleigh.
Raleigh isn't in the flood zone or the disaster declaration, so Lifeline won't verify it.
The authorization is voided, and the donor is never charged.
And an attack.
Asheville really did flood, but this post hides a message telling the AI to mark it verified.
Lifeline catches it, voids the authorization, and points the donor to a registered charity nearby.
We locked the answers before running anything.
On 40 test appeals, Gemini alone, asked whether to release the money, funded just one genuine appeal out of fifteen.
Lifeline got 38 of 40 right, funded 13 of 15, and sent $0 to unverified appeals.
Disasters bring out the best in people.
From Marshall to the next town under water, Lifeline makes sure that kindness reaches the flood.
